newsitem.title: UK: Guinness repeats stance on buybacks.
newsitem.headline: Guinness repeats stance on buybacks.

text.p: British Drinks group Guinness Plc on repeated its policy stance on any future plans to buy back its own shares on Thursday.
Many investors and analysts expect the company to announce a further buyback of 100 million shares shortly.

The company announced a buy-back of shares worth 460 million stg, representing five percent of the company, the day after its 1995 results. Earlier today Guinness posted an 11 percent increase in its 1996 pre-tax profits to 975 million stg.

"We reitereated in our press release that we would return funds surplus to the needs of the business to shareholders and the board will take that action at the approporate time and in a way that they feel is appropriate," said chairman Tony Greener in an interview.

Guinness, which generates a substantial level of free cash flow, is not committed to either an extreme dividend policy or paying down high debt levels as seen at Allied Domecq and Grand Metropolitan Plc respectively.
Guinness generated 408 million stg of free cash flow before dividends in 1996, giving a total of 2.2 billion over the last five years.
"I think I would make the point, however, that our record in this area (returning cash to shareholders) is very strong," said Greener.
"If you look at our dividend performance over the last five years our dividend is up by about 50 percent which is double the rate of the average for the FTSE.
"In addition to that we returned half a billion pounds to shareholders last year and we have already done 200 million stg this year," he added.
